items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: I first heard Red Nichols and his Five Pennies with Jimmy Dorsey on the clarinet

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you something that I’d like to relate to our students. You know, many times people didn’t understand how necessary jam sessions were but that’s where you could work out your ideas. Tell us about jam sessions.

We used to do quite a lot of that, get together and play. I know that when I was just learning the bass we’d go into the auditorium when nothing was happening, go down to the bottom of the auditorium there and this trombone player and I would play tunes. He was just learning “Jazz Me Blues” and tunes like that, and I was just learning the bass, I had just learned the scale. So I was learning to play in B flat. He showed me the C scale. And then I went from there, the first Saturday night I got a job on the bass,…
Is there anybody today that is playing the bass the way that you like to hear it played?
